title: Area of a triangle
summary: A right triangle is half a rectangle: that's why you divide by two.

steps.text: Cut a rectangle along its diagonal and you get two equal triangles. Each one is half. ✂️

steps.caption: This right triangle is half of a $4$ by $3$ rectangle.

steps.prompt: The $4 \times 3$ rectangle has area $12$. What is the area of the triangle?

feedback.correct: That's it! The triangle is half: $12 \div 2 = 6$.
feedback.incorrect: The triangle is half of the rectangle. What is half of $12$?

hints: The triangle fills half the rectangle.

steps.text: Hence the formula: area of a triangle $= \dfrac{\text{base} \times \text{height}}{2}$.

steps.prompt: What is the area of a triangle with base $6$ and height $4$?

feedback.incorrect: Multiply base by height and divide by $2$: $\frac{6 \times 4}{2}$.

steps.prompt: What is the area of a triangle with base $10$ and height $5$?

steps.text: Base times height over two. And the 'over two' is only because a triangle is half a rectangle. 🎉
